claim: The proposed IoT ECG monitoring system uses the AD8232 single-lead ECG front-end IC with AgCl gel electrodes paired with an ESP32 microcontroller for signal acquisition and Wi-Fi transmission.
stance_target: AD8232 + ESP32 is a viable low-cost architecture for a B.Tech biomedical ECG project
quoted_support: The ECG signal is obtained using an AD8232 ECG monitoring with AgCl gel electrode as well as a Node MCU microcontroller with inside-the-chip Wi-Fi.

claim: The system streams ECG, body temperature, alcohol level, and pulse data to the Blynk IoT cloud dashboard for real-time viewing by clinicians and caregivers, with an AMOLED display and GSM-based alarms locally.
stance_target: system architecture for cloud-connected ECG monitor
scope_conditions: proposed methodology section of the paper
quoted_support: The ESP32 capabilities an onboard Wi-Fi module that engages the information it has extracted to the Blynk web system.

claim: Cardiovascular disease risk factors are highly prevalent in some developing-country populations, cited as 99.6% of males and 97.9% of females in Bangladesh having at least one identified CVD risk factor.
stance_target: motivation for low-cost remote ECG monitoring in developing regions
scope_conditions: Bangladesh, cited from prior literature not primary data collected by this paper
quoted_support: Bangladesh has one of the greatest cases of cardiovascular disease (CVD) among developing countries, with 99.6% of the male population and 97.9% of the female population having at least one identified CVD risk factor.

claim: A prior openMSP430-based wearable signal-processing system achieved a 10x reduction in response time compared to earlier approaches.
stance_target: microcontroller choice affects responsiveness of wearable ECG systems
scope_conditions: cited prior work [9], not independently verified by this paper
quoted_support: The installation outcomes indicate a 10 times reduction in time to response

claim: A prior ESP32+AD8232 Bluetooth smartphone ECG monitor design (cited as related work) has documented limits in accuracy and reliability for high-risk individuals, motivating future noise-reduction filtering.
stance_target: ESP32+AD8232 designs are already fully reliable for clinical-grade ECG monitoring
quoted_support: it has limits in both accuracy and reliability for individuals with increased risk. Future research may target noise reduction filters to increase system accuracy and dependability
